structured_output.analysis:
Every proposal from round 1 was refused because its rationale used a rounded KL value that does not appear in any record. This round, rationales only use exact numbers from cited records. There is almost no spare bit budget: the best recipe averages 3.147953869047619 bits per weight against a limit of 403/128. Any layer upgrade therefore has to be paid for. The analysis has no per-layer data showing which layers are cheap to downgrade. So the layer-upgrade grid pays by raising the rht_gptq_int3 group size to 256, which costs no layer downgrades. The other two grids change GPTQ settings only (act_order, damp), which costs no bits. Expected gains:
- 27.mlp.up_proj: gptq_int3 to gptq_int4 cuts KL from 0.0057182 to 0.00216589.
- 27.mlp.gate_proj: rht_gptq_int3 to rht_gptq_int4 cuts it from 0.00498703 to 0.00153131.
- 14.mlp.down_proj: rht_gptq_int2 to rht_gptq_int3 cuts it from 0.00633466 to 0.00181478.

proposals.name: act_order_all_gptq
proposals.rationale: Uses the same layer assignment as the measured iso_3.15 (E514ab09c524e) and turns on act_order=true for every GPTQ-family method, so the bit cost is unchanged. GPTQ layers carry the largest losses, for example gptq_int3 on 27.mlp.up_proj at 0.0057182 (Ef04d8aa7bded) and rht_gptq_int2 on 14.mlp.down_proj at 0.00633466 (E4c3f9b73e065). Act-order quantization is meant to reduce error on these layers.

proposals.name: damp_high_all_gptq
proposals.rationale: Uses the same assignment as iso_3.15 (E514ab09c524e) with damp=0.05 for all GPTQ-family methods, so the bit cost is unchanged. This tests whether stronger Hessian damping generalizes better to the validation windows. The measured whole-recipe KL of iso_3.15 is worse than its single-layer prediction (E514ab09c524e), which suggests overfitting to calibration.

proposals.name: top3_upgrades_rht3_g256
proposals.rationale: Upgrades three of the highest-loss layers. 27.mlp.up_proj goes from gptq_int3 to gptq_int4, cutting KL from 0.0057182 (Ef04d8aa7bded) to 0.00216589 (Efea8c18d2abc). 27.mlp.gate_proj goes from rht_gptq_int3 to rht_gptq_int4, cutting it from 0.00498703 (Efa0bb391da67) to 0.00153131 (Ef428ac081334). 14.mlp.down_proj goes from rht_gptq_int2 to rht_gptq_int3, cutting it from 0.00633466 (E4c3f9b73e065) to 0.00181478 (E90bd4b2f3645). The extra bits are paid for by setting group_size=256 on rht_gptq_int3, which halves the per-group scale overhead.
